6163.stem:
A surveyor makes a field trip to survey a proposed subdivision of some land for a developer. He returns with this field diagram.

\exfigure{719_q23_1}

figures.cap: field diagram with bearings 316, 058, 125, 238 and distances 84, 57, 62, 77
solution sketch: field diagram in guidelines (different version of Q23) with 58 degree angle marked

parts.latex: Calculate the area of the subdivision to the nearest square metre.
parts.note: Owner 25 Nov: "Also a trig question was also pulled into a measurement Y11 exam? how is that possible": radial survey with A = 1/2 ab sin C is Year 12 Trigonometry (S2-12-070 main, S2-12-068), not Year 11 measurement only

parts.latex:
The developer needs at least 550 square metres for each section of the subdivision. Also, the local council needs 10% of the land for the required infrastructure.

What is the maximum number of sections the developer could make from his land development?

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{719_q23_s1}

The angles at $O$ between neighbouring rays are the differences of the bearings:
$$\begin{aligned} \angle AOB &= 360^\circ-316^\circ+58^\circ = 102^\circ \\ \angle BOC &= 125^\circ-58^\circ = 67^\circ \\ \angle COD &= 238^\circ-125^\circ = 113^\circ \\ \angle DOA &= 316^\circ-238^\circ = 78^\circ \end{aligned}$$
Using $A=\dfrac12ab\sin C$ for each triangle:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac12(84)(57)\sin102^\circ+\dfrac12(57)(62)\sin67^\circ+\dfrac12(62)(77)\sin113^\circ+\dfrac12(77)(84)\sin78^\circ \\ &= 2341.68\ldots+1626.53\ldots+2197.24\ldots+3163.32\ldots \\ &= 9328.79\ldots \\ &\approx 9329 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds $\angle AOB$ and substitutes into the area formula, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Source drawing kept.
meta.corrected: Corrected from source: the school worked another version of the question (area of triangle $AOB$ only, $2342$ m$^2$); the subdivision is all four triangles, $9329$ m$^2$.
meta.overwritten_from_source: Corrected from source: the school worked another version of the question (area of triangle $AOB$ only, $2342$ m$^2$); the subdivision is all four triangles, $9329$ m$^2$.
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

solutions.latex:
The council takes $10\%$, leaving $90\%$ of the land.
$$0.90 \times 9329 = 8396.1 \text{ m}^2$$
$$\dfrac{8396.1}{550} = 15.26\ldots$$
Only whole sections of at least $550 \text{ m}^2$ count, so round down.
$$\therefore\ 15 \text{ sections}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us (source had none). Source wrote '3 parts'; changed to sections.
meta.corrected: Corrected from source: follows from the whole area: $0.9\times9329\div550=15.26$, so $15$ sections, not $3$.
meta.overwritten_from_source: Corrected from source: follows from the whole area: $0.9\times9329\div550=15.26$, so $15$ sections, not $3$.
meta.final_by: claude-sonnet-5-5 26 Nov (read from the worked solution)

7670.stem:
A partially complete radial survey of a park is shown in the diagram below.

\exfigure{2843_q3e_1}

figures.cap: radial survey with X (053 degrees), Z (270 degrees), Y and centre O

parts.latex:
The area of the $\triangle XOY$ is $1374\ \text{m}^2$.

Calculate the true bearing of $Y$ from $O$, correct to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula for a triangle,
$$A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$$
Substituting $A = 1374$, $a = 54$, $b = 60$ and $C = \theta$:
$$\begin{aligned} 1374 &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 54\times 60\times\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta &= \dfrac{1374}{\frac{1}{2}\times 54\times 60} \\ \theta &= 58^\circ \end{aligned}$$
The bearing of $Y$ is the bearing of $X$ plus $\theta$:
$$\text{Bearing} = 53 + 58 = 111^\circ$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the true bearing of } Y \text{ from } O \text{ is } 111^\circ$$
criteria: Finds the angle $\theta$, or equivalent merit
Correct substitution into the area formula, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: The sketch_id is not used as a solution drawing was not required.

2843_q3e_1.notes: Radial survey: outer triangle ZXY plus the radials OZ, OX and OY, at the crop's vertex positions. The labels are X 053°, Z 270°, O, Y and 45 m, 54 m, 60 m; the point letters are in maths italic. Lines 0.6pt. Rules 1, 3, 6a, 19.

7796.stem:
A radial compass survey of a sports centre is shown in the diagram

\exfigure{708_q32_1}

figures.cap: radial compass survey with points A 320, B 074, C 195 from O

parts.latex: Show that the size of angle $AOB$ is $114^\circ$
Find the area of triangle $AOB$ in hectares, correct to two significant figures.

solutions.latex:
The bearing of $A$ is $320^\circ$, so $A$ is $360 - 320 = 40^\circ$ west of north.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle AOB &= 74^\circ + (360 - 320)^\circ \\ &= 74^\circ + 40^\circ \\ &= 114^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Solution diagram not added (question's own figure used).

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula for a triangle,
$$A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$$
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 287 \times 211 \times \sin 114^\circ \\ &= 27\,660.78614 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
Since $1 \text{ ha} = 10\,000 \text{ m}^2$,
$$\therefore\ \text{area} \approx 2.8 \text{ ha}$$
criteria: Finds the area in $\text{m}^2$, or equivalent merit
Substitutes into the area formula, or equivalent merit

708_q32_1.notes: Radial survey: solid OA, OB, OC with rotated lengths 287 m, 211 m, 295 m, dashed (aux) triangle ABC, North arrow with filled head, bearing labels A 320°, B 074°, C 195°, O, and NOT TO SCALE, at \small to match the crop. In the crop 'North' sits above the arrow tip, where the label would touch dashed line AB, so it is placed beside the arrow (right of the shaft) instead. A third render was needed only to clear that label check. Label check passes. Remaining overlay difference is label glyph placement. Rules 1, 3, 4, 11.

7830.stem:
A partially complete radial survey of a park is shown in the diagram below.

\exfigure{2841_q1d_1}

figures.cap: radial survey: O with A (043 degrees, 42 m), C (316 degrees, 48 m), B (56 m)
solution sketch: radial survey annotated with angles 44, 43 and theta

parts.latex: Find the area of $\Delta OAC$, correct to 1 decimal place.
Given that $AB = 84.3$ m, find the bearing of $B$ from $O$, to the nearest degree.

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula $A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$,
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}\times 48\times 42\times\sin 87^\circ \\ &\approx 1006.6 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ A \approx 1006.6 \text{ m}^2$$
criteria: Correct area formula substitution, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in $\triangle OAB$ to find $\theta = \angle AOB$,
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{56^2 + 42^2 - 84.3^2}{2\times 56\times 42}$$
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(\text{Ans}) \approx 118^\circ$$
The bearing adds the $43^\circ$ bearing of the reference line.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{bearing} &= 118 + 43 \\ &= 161^\circ \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{bearing} = 161^\circ$$
criteria: Correct cosine rule substitution, or equivalent merit

2841_q1d_1.notes: Radial survey: O joined to A, B and C; outer triangle CAB; N arrow drawn with a filled Latex head (rule 4). Bearing and length labels and NOT TO SCALE are placed as in the crop. N and 56 m moved slightly so they clear the lines (rule 11). Original-side score 0.83 is due to scan stroke thickness and glyph shape.

2841_q1d_s1.notes: Same survey as the solution figure. The teacher's grey handwritten 44, 43 and θ are replaced with clean angle arcs centred at O, each running exactly between its arms: 44° (OC to N), 43° (N to OA) and θ (OA to OB), as the worked solution uses (rules 17, 18, 22). Point letters are in maths italic, not the scan's upright letters (rule 19). Label check passes.

7893.stem:
A radial compass survey of a sports centre is shown in the diagram.

\exfigure{706_q30_1}

parts.latex: Calculate the length of the boundary $AB$, to the nearest metre.
Find the perimeter of triangle $AOB$, correct to two significant figures.

solutions.latex:
Let $D$ be the point directly north of $O$.
$$\angle AOD = 360^\circ - 320^\circ = 40^\circ$$
$$\begin{aligned} \angle AOB &= 74^\circ + 40^\circ \\ &= 114^\circ \end{aligned}$$

Using the cosine rule in $\triangle AOB$:
$$\begin{aligned} AB^2 &= 287^2 + 211^2 - 2 \times 287 \times 211 \times \cos 114^\circ \\ &= 176151.5018\ldots \\ AB &= \sqrt{176151.5018\ldots} \\ &= 419.7040645\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ AB = 420 \text{ m}$$
criteria: Correct cosine rule substitution, or equivalent merit

706_q30_1.notes: Radial survey from O: OA, OB and OC with rotated distance labels, a North arrow, a dashed boundary triangle ABC, bearing labels A 320°, B 074° and C 195°, and NOT TO SCALE. The first draw had C and B placed wrongly. They were moved to the crop's positions in round 2. A 3rd draw nudged the 211 m label off OB. I left out the scan's tiny arrowheads at the ends of the lines. Rules 1, 2, 3, 4, 6a, 11.

7924.stem:
The following diagram shows the results of a radial survey

\exfigure{707_q18d_1}

figures.cap: radial survey with bearings X 309, Y 053, P 147, T 225 from O and distances

parts.latex: What is the size of $\angle XOY$?
Find the area of triangle $XOY$, correct to $2$ decimal places.
Determine the length of $XY$ correct to $3$ significant figures

solutions.latex:
The angle is made up of the part from $309^\circ$ round to north and the part from north to $53^\circ$.
$$\begin{aligned} \angle XOY &= (360 - 309) + 53 \\ &= 104^\circ \end{aligned}$$

meta.format_note: Rubric written by us. Figure not visible.

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula for a triangle:
$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 65 \times 53 \times \sin 104^\circ \\ &\approx 1671.33 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$

Using the cosine rule in triangle $XOY$:
$$\begin{aligned} XY^2 &= 65^2 + 53^2 - 2 \times 65 \times 53 \times \cos 104^\circ \\ &= 8700.841\ldots \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} XY &= \sqrt{8700.841\ldots} \\ &= 93.2783\ldots \\ &\approx 93.3 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes correctly into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

707_q18d_1.notes: Radial survey: four rays from O, positioned as in the crop (marked NOT TO SCALE, so the bearings are not drawn to true angle; rule 1). Labels: X 309°, Y 053°, T 225°, P 147°, the distances 65, 53, 61 and 49 m, and 'Not to scale'. The point letters are maths italic, not the original's upright sans-serif (rule 19). The small scan breaks on the rays are not copied. The overlay is low because the label fonts differ and the labels were moved off the rays (rule 11); the line geometry matches.

7943.stem:
A radial survey of land DEFG is shown below:

\exfigure{3295_q7a_1}

figures.cap: radial survey with bearings and distances from O to D, E, F, G

parts.latex: What is the size of $\angle DOG$ ?
What is the length of DG correct to the nearest metre?
What is the area of triangle of DOG correct to the nearest square metre?

solutions.latex:
Using the cosine rule in triangle $DOG$, with $x = DG$:
$$\begin{aligned} x^2 &= 48^2 + 49^2 - 2 \times 48 \times 49 \times \cos 70^\circ \\ &\approx 3096.137 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} x &\approx 55.642 \\ &\approx 56 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct substitution into the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

3295_q7a_1.notes: Radial survey from O: the five rays (North arrow plus D, E, F, G) at the crop's angles and lengths, with bearing and distance labels as printed. The North arrow is 0.6pt (rule 3), not bold as in the crop. E is now maths italic like the other points (rule 19). Fixed in round 2: D ray end and the 49 m label, which had touched the line. What is left in the overlay is font-width difference only. Rules 1, 3, 4, 6a, 11, 19.
